evidence: Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī
Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam
terms.comment: What happens as a rule, though not always: plērumque enim nōn semper ēveniunt (Cic. Div. 2.14, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 9.26.8: nōn nōminātim, sed in ūniversum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Taken as a whole, as against one by one; Livy and Tacitus, not Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.66: omnīnō fortis animus et magnus duābus rēbus maximē cernitur
terms.comment: At the head of a general statement (Lewis & Short); its usual sense is “altogether, at all”.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.10: fit ferē ut (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.143: generātim atque ūniversē loquī (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō
phrases.english: I wake when I like, generally about the first hour, often before, rarely later

phrases.latin: terra etsī aliquantō speciē differt, in ūniversum tamen aut silvīs horrida aut palūdibus foeda
phrases.english: the land, though it varies somewhat in appearance, is in general either bristling with forests or foul with marshes

sources: Lewis & Short: plerumque · Lewis & Short: universus · Lewis & Short: omnino · Lewis & Short: fere · Lewis & Short: universe
